wordings.WINDOW_ROTARY_TITLE: \text{Rotary Embedding of a Sliding Window Layer}
wordings.PAIRS_OF_THE_TURNED_CHANNELS: The 64 turned channels of a head are taken two at a time as points in a plane, and the rotation turns each point about the origin.
wordings.TURN_BY_THE_TOKEN: The angle of the turn grows with the position of the token, and each pair of channels turns at a speed of its own.
wordings.SCORE_BY_DISTANCE: A query and a key that are both turned score against each other by how far apart their tokens are, because the product of two turned points depends on the difference of the two angles.
wordings.TABLE_IN_THE_BOX: The circle in the box is the table of turns, which holds one turn for every position and every pair of channels.
wordings.HALVES_OF_THE_REFERENCE: The reference holds the 64 turned channels of a head as two halves, the real parts of the 32 pairs and then their imaginary parts, so channel i of the first half and channel i of the second half are one pair. The projection before the box writes the two halves into its rows, and the covariant view named Pairs writes them in the order of the pairs. The reference writes the turned pairs back as two halves, where the box writes each pair back in place. The query and the key are written in the same order, so every score is unchanged.
FULL_ROTATION_DESCRIPTION: Each vector is turned by the position of its token. The operation is called a rotary embedding.
The full attention layers read the table built at the base rope_theta, 10,000,000, and turn the first 64 channels of every query head and every key head this way.
WINDOW_ROTATION_DESCRIPTION: Each vector is turned by the position of its token, as in the full attention layers.
The sliding window layers read a second table, built at the base swa_rope_theta, 10,000. A smaller base turns every pair faster, and the window reads no key further than 127 tokens back.
wordings.PAIRS_MERGE_DESCRIPTION: Writes the two halves of the turned channels in the order of the pairs, the real part of pair i at channel 2i and its imaginary part at channel 2i + 1. The reference holds the real parts of the 32 pairs in the first 32 channels and their imaginary parts in the last 32, which is the layout rotate_half reads.
wordings.CHANNEL_JOIN_DESCRIPTION: Joins two runs of channels into one vector. The second run comes after the first, so the size of the result is the sum of the sizes of the two runs. A query head and a key head each join their 64 turned channels and their 128 other channels into 192, with the turned channels first, as the torch.cat of the reference does.
wordings.PAIRS_AS_COMPLEX_DESCRIPTION: Reads every two adjacent channels as one complex number, with the first channel as the real part and the second as the imaginary part. A complex number is a point in a plane. Multiplying the point by a complex number of length one turns it about the origin, so the rotation of a pair is one product. The covariant view named Pairs before it writes the two halves of the reference in this order.
wordings.DECOMPLEX_DESCRIPTION: Writes every complex number as two adjacent channels, the real part first and the imaginary part second. The reference writes the real parts into the first 32 channels and the imaginary parts into the last 32. The query and the key are written in the same order, so every score is unchanged.
wordings.ROTARY_TABLE_ROLE: The table of turns, which holds e^(i x theta) for every position x and every one of the 32 frequencies theta. The frequency of pair j is the base raised to the power -2j/64. The full attention layers build the table at the base rope_theta and the sliding window layers at the base swa_rope_theta.
wordings.ONE_WEIGHT_PER_PART: The reference computes the queries, the keys and the values with one weight, qkv_proj, and cuts the result with torch.split. The expression holds one weight per part.
QUERY_DESCRIPTION: The queries of every token. One projection of the hidden state gives the 64 channels of every query head that the rotary embedding turns, written as the two halves the reference holds them in, and a second gives the 128 channels it passes through. The rotary embedding turns the first part once per head, and the two parts are joined into a query head of 192 channels, the turned channels first. The 128 query heads are written as 8 groups of 16, and the heads of group i read key head i and value head i.
KEY_DESCRIPTION: The keys of every token. There are 8 key heads, one for each group of 16 query heads. Each key head is built as a query head is built: 64 turned channels and 128 channels passed through, joined into 192 with the turned channels first.
VALUE_DESCRIPTION: The values of every token, 8 value heads of 128 channels, one for each group of 16 query heads. The reference multiplies every value by attention_value_scale, 0.612, before it caches the values and before the attention reads them.
wordings.SCORE_STEPS_SENTENCE: The query scores against the key at every slot, and the score is divided by the square root of the width of a head, 192.
wordings.GROUPS_OF_HEADS_SENTENCE: Every query head of a group reads the key head and the value head of its group, which is the repeat_kv of the reference.
CORE_DESCRIPTION: The attention of one query in a full attention layer, computed once per query.
A softmax over the tokens at or before the query gives the weights, and the weights sum the values.
SINK_CORE_DESCRIPTION: The attention of one query in a sliding window layer, computed once per query.

The exponentials of the scores over the 128 slots of the window are summed, and the exponential of a learned logit of the query head is added to the sum. Each exponential of a score is divided by the total, and the quotients weight the values. The logit is called an attention sink. It has no value, so a head can give most of its weight to the sink and take little from the window.
The reference concatenates the logit to the scores, takes the softmax over both and drops the column of the logit, which gives the same weights.
wordings.FULL_ATTENTION_DESCRIPTION: Grouped-query attention over every token at or before the query, in the 10 full attention layers. The queries, the keys and the values are projected from the normalised hidden state, and the keys and the values are read back from every query through the view named Back. The attention core is computed once per query, and the output projection maps the 128 query heads back onto the hidden width.
wordings.WINDOW_ATTENTION_DESCRIPTION: Grouped-query attention over the 128 tokens ending at the query, in the 60 sliding window layers. The queries, the keys and the values are projected from the normalised hidden state, and the keys and the values are read back from every query through the view named Window. The attention core adds the learned logit of every query head to its softmax, and the output projection maps the 128 query heads back onto the hidden width. The keys and the queries are turned by the table of the sliding window layers.
wordings.SWIGLU_STEPS_SENTENCE: The hidden state is projected twice, the SiLU of the first projection multiplies the second, and the product is projected back onto the hidden width.
DENSE_MLP_DESCRIPTION: The feed-forward map of layer 0, a SwiGLU of width 16,384 computed once per token.
wordings.GATE_DESCRIPTION: The router of one token. A linear map of the hidden state and a sigmoid score all 384 experts. A learned correction bias is added to one copy of the scores, and the 8 experts with the largest biased scores are kept. The other copy holds no bias and is read at the 8 kept experts, so the bias decides which experts run and never scales their outputs. The 8 gates are divided by their sum plus 10^-20. The reference computes the router in FP32.
ROUTED_EXPERTS_DESCRIPTION: The 8 experts chosen for one token, each a SwiGLU of width 2,048 with weights of its own.

The weights produce the expert axis, so the implicit weight of each projection holds all 384 experts, and the diagonalisation after the down projection keeps the output of the expert chosen at each slot.
wordings.MIXTURE_DESCRIPTION: The mixture of experts of one token, computed once per token in layers 1 to 69. The gate chooses 8 of the 384 experts and weights them, the chosen experts run, and one contraction over the 8 slots multiplies every output by its gate and sums the products. The mixture has no shared expert.
wordings.RESIDUAL_DESCRIPTION: Normalises the hidden state with an RMS normalisation, passes the result through the sublayer, and adds the output of the sublayer to the hidden state from before the normalisation. Every layer holds two of these, one around the attention and one around the feed-forward map.
wordings.FIRST_LAYER_DESCRIPTION: Layer 0, the one layer with the dense MLP. It attends with full attention.
wordings.WINDOW_LAYERS_DESCRIPTION: A run of sliding window layers, each with the mixture of experts. The repetition of the block is the length of the run.
wordings.FIRST_GROUP_DESCRIPTION: Layers 1 to 7: six sliding window layers followed by one full attention layer, every one of them with the mixture of experts.
wordings.LONG_GROUPS_DESCRIPTION: Layers 8 to 55, six repetitions of seven sliding window layers followed by one full attention layer, every one of them with the mixture of experts. The full attention layers are 15, 23, 31, 39, 47 and 55.
wordings.LAST_GROUPS_DESCRIPTION: Layers 56 to 69, two repetitions of six sliding window layers followed by one full attention layer, every one of them with the mixture of experts. The full attention layers are 62 and 69.
wordings.EMBEDDING_BLOCK_DESCRIPTION: Looks every token identifier up in a table of 152,576 rows of 6,144 channels. The reference replaces the rows of the image, video and audio tokens of a prompt with the outputs of its encoders, which the expression does not hold.
wordings.OUTPUT_DESCRIPTION: Normalises the final hidden state with an RMS normalisation and maps it onto one logit for every entry of the vocabulary. The output head has a weight of its own, because tie_word_embeddings is false.
wordings.TOP_K_EXPERTS_DESCRIPTION: Keeps the 8 largest of the 384 biased scores of a token and hands them out on a sparse axis over the experts, which holds a value at the 8 kept experts and nothing at the others.
wordings.SELECT_DESCRIPTION: Reads the unbiased scores at the experts the top-8 kept. The value the top-8 hands out at a kept expert is the indicator of a positive biased score, which is 1 for every expert the released router can keep, so every gate is the unbiased score.
wordings.EMBEDDING_DESCRIPTION: Reads the row of the table named by the token identifier.
wordings.BACK_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Reads the array over the tokens at token i_x - i_r for every distance i_r of every query i_x. A distance counting back past the first token reads the universal unit, so the distance axis leaves the view as r|x, which holds a value where i_x - i_r >= 0. A full attention layer reads its keys and its values through this view, which states the causal mask of the reference.
wordings.WINDOW_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Reads the array over the tokens at token i_x - i_w for every slot i_w of the window of every query i_x, 128 slots with slot 0 at the query itself. A slot counting back past the first token reads the universal unit, so the slot axis leaves the view as w|x, which holds a value where i_x - i_w >= 0. A sliding window layer reads its keys and its values through this view, which states the mask of create_sliding_window_causal_mask in transformers: key k is kept for query q where q - 128 < k <= q.
wordings.DIAGONAL_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Keeps the entries of the down projection where the slot and the expert agree, so each slot holds the output of the expert chosen there.
wordings.QUERY_TURNED_PROJECTION_ROLE: The rows of qkv_proj that give the 64 turned channels of every query head.
wordings.QUERY_UNTURNED_PROJECTION_ROLE: The rows of qkv_proj that give the 128 channels of every query head that the rotary embedding passes through.
wordings.KEY_TURNED_PROJECTION_ROLE: The rows of qkv_proj that give the 64 turned channels of every key head.
wordings.KEY_UNTURNED_PROJECTION_ROLE: The rows of qkv_proj that give the 128 channels of every key head that the rotary embedding passes through.
wordings.VALUE_PROJECTION_ROLE: The rows of qkv_proj that give the 128 channels of every value head.
wordings.OUTPUT_PROJECTION_ROLE: o_proj, which maps the outputs of the 128 query heads back onto the hidden width.
wordings.SINK_ROLE: attention_sink_bias, one learned logit for every query head of a sliding window layer. It joins the softmax of the head with no value.
wordings.ROUTER_ROLE: The weight of the router, which scores every expert from the hidden state.
wordings.CORRECTION_BIAS_ROLE: e_score_correction_bias, one number per expert, added to the scores that choose the experts and to no gate. In the checkpoint the biases lie between -0.349 and 0.810, and at least 344 of the 384 are positive in every layer.
wordings.EXPERT_GATE_PROJECTION_ROLE: gate_proj of every routed expert, stacked over the 384 experts.
wordings.EXPERT_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: up_proj of every routed expert, stacked over the 384 experts.
wordings.EXPERT_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: down_proj of every routed expert, stacked over the 384 experts.
wordings.DENSE_GATE_PROJECTION_ROLE: gate_proj of the dense MLP of layer 0.
wordings.DENSE_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: up_proj of the dense MLP of layer 0.
wordings.DENSE_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: down_proj of the dense MLP of layer 0.
wordings.OUTPUT_HEAD_ROLE: lm_head, which maps the final hidden state onto one logit for every entry of the vocabulary.
wordings.ATTENTION_SCALE_ROLE: The scale of the scores, one over the square root of the width of a query head, 192.
wordings.VALUE_SCALE_ROLE: The value scale attention_value_scale, 0.612, which multiplies every value before the reference caches it.
wordings.ROUTER_SIGMOID_ROLE: The sigmoid that turns the logit of every expert into a score between 0 and 1.
wordings.SILU_ROLE: The SiLU of the gate projection of a SwiGLU.
wordings.INDICATOR_ROLE: The indicator of a positive biased score, which marks the experts the top-8 kept.
wordings.RECIPROCAL_ROLE: The reciprocal of the sum of the exponentials of the scores and of the sink, which divides every exponential of a score.
